source: drafts are hand-written; picks are real products (picks.json)

expect_semantics.fail: at least one of fails_any fires (hard)
expect_semantics.known_gap: the case PASSES today although the draft is bad; it documents a residual. If a rule change closes the gap, flip the expectation and remove known_gap

check_ids: C0 C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 C7 C8 C8d C8d-x (hard); C8c OUR SOFT SPACED_DASH (warn)
note: X2 is a unit test of the gate on URLs; X1 and X3 tamper with a rendered page. A foreign image can only reach the page through a renderer or snapshot bug, so these are tripwires.

cases.title: the pick's own image URL with a different ?v=
cases.note: an exact string match would wrongly fail it

cases.title: a real image of another product (not a pick of this draft)
cases.note: passes the host, prefix and snapshot tests; only the per-pick lookup catches it

cases.title: same filename under another store prefix
userinfo trick: cdn.shopify.com@evil.io
cases.note: a string startswith check passes it

cases.title: a redirect parameter in the query
cases.note: stripping the query before the check would pass it

cases.title: path traversal
cases.note: normalising before the check can launder it

cases.title: a plausible www.nicobar.com/cdn/shop/files path
cases.note: the only "on nicobar.com" form that is not in the snapshot

cases.title: file name in lower case
cases.note: path is case-sensitive; whether Shopify is case-insensitive is unknown

cases.title: host in upper case
cases.note: a URL parser lower-cases the host

cases.title: an image shared by two products, draft selects the first owner
the same shared image, draft selects the second owner
the same shared image, draft selects neither owner
a correct render of the known-good email passes X1, X2 and X3

email.subject: Evenings for the festive table
email.preheader: A dupatta, a shawl and trousers for wedding lunches and Diwali evenings.
email.body: The festive table, and the evenings around it. {p1} is made in metallic tissue, free-size and light enough to layer over any festive kurta. Wear it over teal, purple or pink for wedding lunches and Diwali evenings. {p2} is woven in 100% wool, with gota flowers and leaves worked into the corners. Saanjh means dusk, and the colour is meant to glow like it. {p3} is 100% linen in a bottom weight, piece dyed in a natural beige called sand.
